question: Under Colorado Revised Statutes § 12-10-101(2), what does 'Division' mean as used in Title 12, Article 10?
choice_a: The division of real estate
choice_b: The real estate commission created in section 12-10-206
choice_c: The director of the division of real estate
choice_d: An association formed as part of a common interest community
explanation: Section 12-10-101(2) defines 'Division' to mean the division of real estate. The other options are the text's separate definitions of 'Commission,' 'Director,' and 'HOA,' respectively.

question: Per § 12-10-101(3), which best defines 'HOA' or 'homeowners' association'?
choice_a: Any brokerage firm licensed to employ associate brokers
choice_b: An association or unit owners' association formed before, on, or after July 1, 1992, as part of a common interest community
choice_c: The real estate commission created in section 12-10-206
choice_d: A recognized depository insured by the FDIC or NCUA
explanation: Section 12-10-101(3) defines 'HOA' or 'homeowners' association' as an association or unit owners' association formed before, on, or after July 1, 1992, as part of a common interest community as defined in section 38-33.3-103.

question: Broker Maria is shown in Colorado Real Estate Commission records as employing another broker, Tom. Under § 12-10-201(2), what term describes Maria's status?
choice_a: Designated Broker
choice_b: Supervisory Broker
choice_c: Employing real estate broker (employing broker)
choice_d: Independent Broker
explanation: Section 12-10-201(2) defines 'Employing real estate broker' or 'employing broker' as a broker who is shown in commission records as employing or engaging another broker, which matches Maria's situation with Tom.

question: Which of the following best matches the statutory definition of 'option dealer' under § 12-10-201(4)?
choice_a: A person licensed solely to negotiate residential leases
choice_b: A broker who exclusively represents buyers in exchange for stock options
choice_c: An attorney-in-fact acting under a power of attorney to sell real property
choice_d: A person, firm, partnership, LLC, association, or corporation that takes, obtains, or uses an option to purchase, exchange, rent, or lease real property with intent to buy, sell, exchange, rent, or lease it to others
explanation: Section 12-10-201(4) defines 'option dealer' as any person, firm, partnership, LLC, association, or corporation that directly or indirectly takes, obtains, or uses an option to purchase, exchange, rent, or lease real property with the intent of buying, selling, exchanging, renting, or leasing it to another.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(a), which of the following acts, when performed for compensation, is specifically enumerated as making a person a 'real estate broker'?
choice_a: Auctioning or offering, attempting, or agreeing to auction real estate for compensation
choice_b: Serving as a receiver appointed by a court to manage property
choice_c: Acting as attorney-in-fact under an uncompensated power of attorney
choice_d: Acting personally as principal in acquiring an interest in real estate
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(a)(VI) lists auctioning or offering, attempting, or agreeing to auction real estate as one of the enumerated acts that constitutes 'real estate broker' activity; the other three options are exemptions listed under (6)(b).

question: Negotiating the sale of a business opportunity that involves a change in real estate ownership generally falls within the 'real estate broker' definition under § 12-10-201(6)(a)(IX). This provision exempts the act only when performed by:
choice_a: Any attorney-at-law representing a client
choice_b: A licensed securities broker-dealer under Title 11, article 51, actually engaged generally in the securities business, or their authorized representative
choice_c: A public official conducting official duties
choice_d: A receiver acting under court authorization
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(a)(IX) excludes from broker activity a broker-dealer licensed under article 51 of title 11 who is actually engaged generally in offering, selling, purchasing, or trading securities, or an authorized representative of such a broker-dealer.

question: A person solicits a fee from someone other than a prospective tenant for furnishing information about available rental property. Under § 12-10-201(6)(a)(X), this activity is exempt from the 'real estate broker' definition, but only:
choice_a: If the person is a licensed property manager
choice_b: If the fee is under $100
choice_c: With respect to furnishing information concerning the availability of real property
choice_d: If the transaction involves commercial property only
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(a)(X) states that this exemption 'applies only in respect to the furnishing of information concerning the availability of real property.'

question: Which of the following is exempt from the 'real estate broker' definition under § 12-10-201(6)(b)?
choice_a: An attorney-in-fact acting for compensation under a power of attorney
choice_b: A property manager collecting rent for multiple owners
choice_c: A licensed broker acting as an option dealer
choice_d: An attorney-at-law in connection with representing clients in the practice of law
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(b)(V) exempts an attorney-at-law in connection with representation of clients in the practice of law. Note that the attorney-in-fact exemption in (6)(b)(I) only applies when acting WITHOUT compensation, making option A incorrect.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(b)(VII), a natural person who is a general partner of a partnership or manager of an LLC may sell or lease property owned by that partnership or LLC without triggering the broker license requirement if that person:
choice_a: Owns twenty percent or more of the partnership or limited liability company
choice_b: Holds a real estate degree
choice_c: Has five years of property management experience
choice_d: Is also a licensed contractor
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(b)(VII) exempts a natural person who is a general partner of a partnership, a manager of an LLC, or an owner of twenty percent or more of such partnership or LLC, authorized to sell or lease its property.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(b)(VIII), the corporate-officer exemption applies only if 'officers or regularly salaried employees' derive what minimum percentage of their compensation from the corporation in the form of salaries?
choice_a: At least 50 percent
choice_b: At least 75 percent
choice_c: At least 60 percent
choice_d: 100 percent
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(b)(VIII) defines 'officers or regularly salaried employees' as persons regularly employed who derive not less than seventy-five percent of their compensation from the corporation in the form of salaries.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(b)(IX), a principal officer owning 20% or more of a corporation's stock is generally exempt from the 'real estate broker' definition for company-owned Colorado property, except when the corporation is selling:
choice_a: Commercial office buildings
choice_b: Vacant land
choice_c: Previously occupied one-family and two-family dwellings
choice_d: Industrial parks
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(b)(IX) states this exemption 'does not include any corporation selling previously occupied one-family and two-family dwellings.'

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(b)(X), a property owner is exempt from the 'real estate broker' definition when selling a building it constructed, provided that:
choice_a: The building has been previously occupied and the price excludes the land
choice_b: The building has NOT been previously occupied and the consideration paid for the property includes the cost of the building, payable at conveyance
choice_c: The builder uses a licensed broker to market the property
choice_d: The sale price exceeds $500,000
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(b)(X) exempts an owner selling a commercial, industrial, or residential building on its property 'that has not been previously occupied and where the consideration paid for the property includes the cost of the building, payable, less deposit or down payment, at the time of conveyance.'

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(b)(XI), officers, partners, or managers of a corporation selling a shopping center, office building, or industrial park it owns are exempt from the broker definition only if:
choice_a: They receive no additional compensation for the sale beyond their regular role
choice_b: They receive a sales commission in addition to their salary
choice_c: The property is located outside Colorado
choice_d: The property was previously occupied
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(b)(XI) limits this exemption to officers, partners, or managers 'receiving no additional compensation therefor' when the property is sold, leased, or offered in the ordinary course of the corporation's business.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(b)(XIII), the on-site manager exemption for condominium units defines 'owner' to include:
choice_a: A mortgage lender holding a lien on the units
choice_b: A homeowners' association formed and acting pursuant to its recorded condominium declaration and bylaws
choice_c: A property management company under contract
choice_d: Any tenant association within the building
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(b)(XIII) states that for purposes of this exemption, 'owner' includes a homeowners' association formed and acting pursuant to its recorded condominium declaration and bylaws.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(b)(XIV), an out-of-state real estate broker is exempt from Colorado's 'real estate broker' definition when that broker:
choice_a: Lists Colorado property directly with a Colorado seller
choice_b: Advertises Colorado listings on an out-of-state website
choice_c: Receives a share of a commission or finder's fee on a cooperative transaction from a licensed Colorado real estate broker
choice_d: Manages rental property located in Colorado
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(b)(XIV) exempts a real estate broker licensed in another state who receives a share of a commission or finder's fee on a cooperative transaction from a licensed Colorado real estate broker.

question: Persons negotiating rights-of-way for transportation projects are generally exempt from the 'real estate broker' definition under § 12-10-201(6)(b)(XVI). This exemption does NOT apply when the person:
choice_a: Negotiates easements for water diversion facilities
choice_b: Negotiates telecommunication line easements
choice_c: Negotiates wireless communication facility rights-of-way
choice_d: Represents a displaced person or entity in the purchase, sale, or exchange of real estate resulting from relocations required under a transportation project
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(b)(XVI)(F) conditions the transportation exemption on the person not representing 'any displaced person or entity as an agent thereof in the purchase, sale, or exchange of real estate ... resulting from residential or commercial relocations required under any transportation project.'

question: Under 4 CCR 725-1 Rules 1.1 and 1.27, how does an 'Active' license differ from an 'Inactive' license?
choice_a: An Active license allows a Broker to engage in Real Estate Brokerage Services, while an Inactive license remains valid but does not permit such services
choice_b: Only an Inactive license requires renewal
choice_c: An Inactive license allows unsupervised auctioning of real estate
choice_d: Active and Inactive licenses have identical privileges
explanation: Rule 1.1 defines 'Active' as a current, valid License allowing engagement in Real Estate Brokerage Services, while Rule 1.27 states an Inactive Broker 'holds a valid License' but 'is not permitted to engage in Real Estate Brokerage Services,' though renewal is still required to maintain Inactive status.

question: Broker Jordan holds an Employing Broker level license but continues working under the supervision of another Employing Broker. Under Rule 1.6, how is Jordan classified?
choice_a: Supervisory Broker
choice_b: Associate Broker
choice_c: Designated Broker
choice_d: Team Lead
explanation: Rule 1.6 states that Associate Brokers 'may have an Independent Broker or Employing Broker level license even if they are still acting as an Associate Broker under the supervision of an Employing Broker,' so Jordan remains classified as an Associate Broker.

question: Under Rule 1.8, what must a Brokerage Firm have if it employs or engages Associate Brokers?
choice_a: At least three Employing Brokers
choice_b: A written franchise agreement
choice_c: An Active Employing Broker
choice_d: A Designated Broker in every county where it operates
explanation: Rule 1.8 states 'All Brokerage Firms that employ or engage Associate Brokers must have an Active Employing Broker.'

question: Under Rules 1.52 and 1.53, how do 'Trademark' and 'Trade Name' differ for a Brokerage Firm?
choice_a: A Trademark is the name under which a firm does business other than its legal name, while a Trade Name is a logo or service mark
choice_b: A Trade Name is a logo, service mark, or other identifying mark, while a Trademark is the name used other than the legal name
choice_c: Trademark and Trade Name both refer exclusively to franchise names filed with the Colorado Secretary of State
choice_d: A Trademark is a logo, service mark, or other identifying mark used with the firm's name, while a Trade Name is the name under which the firm does business other than its legal name
explanation: Rule 1.52 defines 'Trademark' as any logo, service mark, or other identifying mark used with a Brokerage Firm's name, while Rule 1.53 defines 'Trade Name' as the name under which a Brokerage Firm does business other than its legal name.

question: Under Rule 1.56, which of the following is one of the minimum required elements of a 'Trust or Escrow Account'?
choice_a: The account is separate and contains only Money Belonging to Others
choice_b: The account may hold both the Broker's personal funds and Money Belonging to Others as long as they are tracked separately
choice_c: The account must earn a minimum interest rate set by the Division
choice_d: The account must be reconciled only once per year
explanation: Rule 1.56 lists as a required element that 'the account is separate and contains only Money Belonging to Others,' along with being custodial/fiduciary, having funds available on demand, and being held with a Recognized Depository.

question: Under Rule 1.35, a 'New Associate Broker' is one who has:
choice_a: Less than one year of licensure regardless of activity status
choice_b: Less than two years of accumulative Active experience
choice_c: No supervising Employing Broker yet assigned
choice_d: Less than five completed transactions
explanation: Rule 1.35 defines a 'New Associate Broker' as 'an Associate Broker with less than two (2) years of accumulative Active experience.'

question: Under Rule 1.44, a 'Recognized Depository' is a bank, savings and loan association, or credit union whose deposits or shares are insured by:
choice_a: The Securities Investor Protection Corporation (SIPC) only
choice_b: A private surety bond company
choice_c: The FDIC or the NCUA
choice_d: The state of Colorado's treasury guarantee fund
explanation: Rule 1.44 defines 'Recognized Depository' as any bank, savings and loan association, or credit union that accepts deposits or shares insured by the FDIC or the NCUA, respectively.

question: Under Rule 1.41, the 'Real Estate Licensing Examination' consists of:
choice_a: A single comprehensive national exam only
choice_b: Three parts: national, state, and ethics
choice_c: A written exam and an oral interview
choice_d: A national part and a Colorado part
explanation: Rule 1.41 defines the 'Real Estate Licensing Examination' as 'an examination that consists of two (2) parts; a national part and a Colorado part as set forth in Rule 2.2.'
